Comment: CloudLab c240g5, U11's worst case on Amazon 300M, with the load held to 900 s. The 360 s runs (4to8-worst-lazy at these rates, 2026-11-22) ended their load with 59-70K queries waiting: from about 200 s on the 4 initial nodes' disks were at their random-read limit (54-60K reads/s), serving their own queries and the new nodes' fetches (55 a query at the end, down 5% every 20 s), and the cluster answered 1910-1945 q/s against 1800 offered, more as the new nodes' raw vectors became local. Extrapolated, the backlog drains at about 560-690 s (lazy-balanced first), which leaves about 210-340 s of keep-up; the new nodes' fetch caches should peak at about two thirds of their bound around 800 s. The run sends about 1.57M of the 2M queries, none repeated; the ground truth covers the first 1M (sent until about 585 s). lazy-balanced runs from this file too (run_one.sh's protocol). Otherwise experiment.amazon-300m-cloudlab-gpu-4to8-worst-lazy.json with this reservation's rates: Rate 900 and at 60 s 1800, from C4 1239 and C8 2483 (2026-11-21).
